newsitem.title: USA: Blue chips retain modest gain after whirlwind session.
newsitem.headline: Blue chips retain modest gain after whirlwind session.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks ended a volatile session with modest gains Friday as the so-called triple-witching options and futures expirations produced the third biggest trading volume ever on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Dow Jones industrial average rose 10.76 points to 6,484.40. In early trading, the Dow rose 75 points to 6,548.99, putting it a shade above its record close of 6,547.79 set on Nov. 25.
For the week, the Dow was up 179.53, its strongest week since the first full week of November, when blue chips began a scorching month-long rally of more than 500 points.

In the broader market, advancing issues swamped declines 1,535 to 968 on very heavy volume of 650 million shares on the NYSE, the third largest total in history and the highest since July 16, when the exchange handled a record 680.3 million shares in volume.
"Today's action and volatility was directly related to options expiration," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.
Even so, analysts said they doubted the market would make much headway next week although individual sectors could see action.

"We'll probably see some more rotation going into the end of the year but we're not going to see much new money," said Robert Froehlich, chief investment strategist at Van Kampen American Capital. "I just think there's not a lot of demand for new stock going into next week."

In contrast to Thursday's session, when a powerhouse rally sent the Dow up 126.87 points for its second biggest point gain ever, the market appeared decidedly cautious, despite an opening blitz of activity in blue-chip stocks.
The trading volume on the NYSE was boosted by the triple-witching expiration of stock options, index options and futures, which triggered huge position-squaring by institutions.
While investors were shying from technology stocks, they were flocking to defensive issues such as banks.
"We saw people getting themselves positioned in classic defensive plays," Froehlich said.
International Business Machines Corp. fell 3-1/2 to 154-5/8, and Intel Corp. lost 2-7/8 to 134-5/8.
"We saw some real profit taking today," said Joseph Battipaglia, chief investment officer at Gruntal & Co.
The big-name stocks were the natural candidates for profit-taking, he said, adding, "If you look at the list of the most widely held stocks, these have been the best performers."
The cautious mood produced a striking disparity between the NYSE and Nasdaq, which is loaded with technology issues.
The Nasdaq Composite index closed 7.30 points lower at 1,288.56.
Dendrite International Inc. plummeted 11-1/2 to 8-1/8, one day after announcing it would lose money in its fourth quarter.
Among banks, J.P. Morgan & Co. climbed 5/8 to 98-5/8 and Chase Manhattan Corp. rose 3/4 to 91-1/2.
Coca-Cola Co. was the NYSE's most active issue, jumping 1-5/8 to 52-7/8 on trading of more than 10 million shares after Salomon Brothers and Lehman Brothers both raised their ratings on the company.
Redhook Ale Brewery Inc. tumbled 4-5/8 to 9-3/8. The company said its fourth quarter results would be below expectations.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 3.11 points to 748.87. The American Stock Exchange index rose 3.48 to 582.01.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 1.95 to 394.11. The average share was up 20 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 7,222.645 up 20.15 or 0.28 percent.
